why_how.text: Orange is the basic color used for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices.
Work-area warning signs are mostly diamond-shaped, although some are rectangular.
Construction and maintenance signs warn of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions near work areas and call for a cautious approach.
Exceeding the posted speed in a construction or work zone is a violation.
The diagonal stripes on barricades or vertical panels show the side on which traffic should pass.
Stripes descending toward the right direct traffic to bear right.
Stripes descending toward the left direct traffic to bear left.
Barricades, panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of work-area hazards and guide traffic, often using steady or flashing lights at night.
Work-zone arrow panels can operate by day or night to guide vehicles into lanes and warn that part of the road ahead is closed.
Work-zone flaggers may stop, slow or guide traffic through the area.
The handbook describes flaggers wearing orange clothing and directing traffic with red flags or stop-and-slow paddles.
Traffic fines are doubled in work zones.
Construction and work zones have no single standard speed limit; the transportation department, local authority, utility company or private contractor sets a limit for each zone.
Knowingly or negligently driving through a highway construction zone in a way that endangers people or property can lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge.
Removing, ignoring or intentionally striking a traffic-control device in the stated highway construction-zone circumstances may also lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge.
